hypothesis: Any affine symplectic transvection fold family that still preserves a symplectic 2-plane slice, even after an arbitrary common linear symplectic left factor, is obstructed by a preserved slice-area bound `R >= delta^(-1/2) >= 1`. If this is correct, the whole slice-preserving/common-left-factor transvection-fold family cannot supply the missing high-density local compressor.
paper_readiness_reason: This attempt adds a new exact obstruction on a genuinely different non-rigid/base-mixing family and backs it with a reproducible numerical audit. It is still not paper-ready because it only rules out the slice-preserving/common-left-factor affine transvection family, does not treat pre-mixing or truly nonlinear plane-destroying models, and does not produce a constructive Hamiltonian.
worked: Implemented `src/transvection_fold_slice_obstruction.py`, a new audit for affine hyperplane folds generated by one-sided symplectic transvections. The script verifies the affine transvection and normalized slice formulas, checks the piecewise Jacobian determinants, establishes the exact slice-area claim `R >= delta^(-1/2) >= 1` for any common linear symplectic left factor, and saves a report to `results/research_loop/attempt_015_transvection_fold_slice_obstruction.json`. It then runs a 5776-case nontrivial grid search over normalized fold parameters `(s,d,lambda)` and a 16-sample random audit of symplectic left factors. The identity baseline saturates the lower bound with sampled radius `1.0`. The best nontrivial refined slice radius is `1.001083448194763` at `(s,d,lambda) = (1.0, 0.9, -0.125)`, with sampled slice area `3.141591421511218` within `1.24e-6` of `pi`. In the mixed audit, the plane coefficient `delta` ranges from `0.2120672840914635` to `0.9834665528801642`, the theoretical lower bound ranges from `1.0083706647215258` to `2.1715166455758785`, the minimum sampled radius is `1.4699275946793848`, the minimum sampled gap above the theoremic bound is `0.1847597220009214`, and the maximum symplectic error of the sampled mixers is `7.080145363731219e-16`.
did_not_work: This more flexible transvection-fold family still does not make the proposed solution correct. The central active slice `D = B^4(1) ∩ E` survives every normalized fold and every common linear symplectic left factor `L` as a planar subset of `L(E)` with symplectic area `pi`. Therefore any containing Euclidean 4-ball must satisfy `R >= delta^(-1/2) >= 1`, where `delta = |omega(f1,f2)|` for an orthonormal basis of `L(E)`. So no member of this family can act as a genuine one-ball compressor. Common linear mixing does not evade the obstruction; unless `L(E)` remains a complex line, it strictly worsens the lower bound because `delta < 1`. A naive attempt to extend the same area-`pi` argument to arbitrary linear pre-factors failed under random pre/post audit, so pre-mixing remains unresolved rather than ruled out.
next_step: Stay on the same broad non-rigid/base-mixing line but leave slice-preserving/common-left-factor transvection folds. The next candidate must destroy every invariant symplectic 2-plane slice, for example via pre-mixing before the fold or a genuinely nonlinear multi-stage local model.
patterns_noticed: Several structural patterns were clean and stable. First, the exact slice-area obstruction is sharp but only trivially so: the identity slice map saturates radius `1`, while every genuinely folded case in the refined search stays strictly above `1`. Second, all 12 refined best nontrivial cases occur at `s = 1.0`; within the searched grid, the active-plane squeeze never helps once a real fold is present. Third, the best nontrivial cases all sit near a shallow seam `d = 0.9` with the smallest nonzero shear magnitude `|lambda| = 0.125`, and the radii then worsen monotonically as `|lambda|` grows or the seam moves deeper into the disk. Fourth, the radius data is symmetric in the sign of `lambda`, as expected from reflection symmetry of the slice. Fifth, the projected slice area in the mixed audit matches the exact formula `pi / delta` to about `1e-5`, so the numerical evidence supports the exact plane-coefficient law rather than merely the weaker `R >= 1` bound. Sixth, common linear symplectic mixing is actively harmful in this family: once the preserved slice plane is tilted away from a complex line, `delta < 1`, the theoretical lower bound jumps above `1`, and the sampled radii jump much higher, with the smallest mixed sampled radius already `1.4699`. The practical design lesson is that any future fold family that leaves a symplectic 2-plane slice invariant up to a common postcomposition factor is structurally doomed; the next live family has to destroy that slice rather than merely disguise it.
notes: No external literature was needed for this step because the obstruction is an internal symplectic-area argument plus numerical audits of the concrete family. The report was rerun after fixing a bookkeeping bug in the affine-formula check, so the saved artifact matches the final script. I also tested a stronger linear pre/post extension inside the same script and rejected it: random pre/post audits showed that the naive claim of an automatic area-`pi` source slice after pre-mixing is false because a non-complex source plane can cut the unit ball with smaller symplectic area. Although the model is piecewise affine rather than smooth, the validated post-factor obstruction itself only uses the preserved active slice and its symplectic area, so the same lower bound still blocks smooth regularizations that preserve such a slice.
